hot.title: Correction Training for Diffusion Models
hot.summary: The authors introduce a learned corrector that repeatedly revises a diffusion denoiser’s clean-image prediction at the same noise level before the next sampling step. On class-conditional ImageNet-256 with DiT-XL/2, correction reaches FID-50K 2.07, versus 9.58 unguided and 2.51 with classifier-free guidance, at about 250 network-function evaluations; it does not outperform guidance on every metric or model.

hot.title: VideoJev: System One Model for Video Understanding and Interaction
hot.summary: VideoJev scores candidate time intervals to locate events and candidate answers for video questions, reusing one video prefix across queries through cached or joint inference. It reports 65.3 mean temporal intersection-over-union, versus 58.6 for its 4B backbone, and a four-benchmark QA mean of 74.3, near 74.9 for Qwen3.5-4B Thinking; evaluations cover grounding and multiple-choice QA, not agent workflows.

hot.title: Vela: User Behavior as Supervision Sparks LLM Intelligence
hot.summary: Vela turns users’ timestamped behavior histories into supervision for predicting future actions and answering rubric-scored questions grounded in past evidence. It separates visible history from future outcomes to avoid leaking prediction targets. Fine-tuning Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on Vela-Instruct raises VelaBench from 51.5 to 63.0, but this shows gains after training on behavior-derived data, not that behavior supervision alone caused them.

hot.title: Open-o3-Video-v2: Seek, Ground, and Reason with Verifiable Spatio-Temporal Evidence
hot.summary: Open-o3-Video-v2 combines iterative video seeking with timestamped object boxes to make retrieved evidence explicit in its reasoning. It requests intervals, inspects frames, and reuses localized evidence in later steps. On V-STaR, its 4B model scores 40.4% mAM and 56.3% mLGM, above its Qwen3-VL-4B backbone; this supports gains in the reported settings, not universal reliability.

hot.title: EgoExplorer: A Vision-Motion-Touch Observatory for Human Loco-Manipulation In Situ
hot.summary: EgoExplorer records continuous whole-body activity by combining five wearable trackers, egocentric video, and articulated hand sensing. Its Calibrate-Complete-Constrain pipeline calibrates body shape and tracker mounts, completes unobserved motion with a temporal prior, and refines it using measurement and geometry constraints. On evaluation, error is 18.0 mm versus 64.1 mm for locally fine-tuned AvatarPoser, against tracker-fitted references, not independent ground truth.

hot.title: Designing Protein Structures from Natural Language
hot.summary: Prompteina lets designers specify global and residue-level protein goals in natural language, then generates structure and sequence together. Its text pathways combine shared context with residue-level control. In a GM2A campaign, 9 of 89 tested designs were classified as binders; the strongest had an apparent dissociation constant of 107 nM across three replicates, validating binding for selected designs against one target.

hot.title: Mitigating Cross-Modal Hallucinations by Correcting Modality Misrouting in Omnimodal LLMs
hot.summary: CaRe addresses audio-visual errors where a correct modality-specific answer is lost in the joint prediction. A text-only probe nominates audio or video; if the unimodal and joint answers disagree, CaRe steers the joint representation toward the unimodal reference while retaining both modalities. On CMM, MiniCPM-o-2.6 reaches 86.9% accuracy versus MAD’s 77.3%; evidence is limited to discrete-answer cross-modal hallucination benchmarks.

hot.title: What Matters in Quality-Aware VLA Pretraining: A Benchmark and Empirical Study
hot.summary: How should demonstration quality be used during vision-language-action (VLA) pretraining to improve performance after target-task fine-tuning? We compare weighting, filtering, and conditioning across reward definitions and label granularities using 5,000 naturally suboptimal human demonstrations and 24 target tasks. Within each VLA, we match demonstrations and training budgets. Additional comparis

hot.title: The Last Remote Sensing Model Built by Humans? Casting Any Earth Observation Task as Recursive Self-Improvement
hot.summary: The system lets a coding agent build Earth-observation models from task data, tools, and compute, using a sealed verifier that returns scores without revealing held-out images or labels. On OpenEarthMap, it reached 60.0 eight-class mIoU from six labeled tiles, versus 34.0 for the starter; with full labels, it scored 71.6, compared with the published 67.5. The six-label result remains below that full-label benchmark.

hot.title: TPPO: Tracking-Value PPO For Language Model Reasoning
hot.summary: TPPO changes PPO’s critic by accumulating position-wise outputs to estimate success probabilities for response prefixes, rather than scoring each independently. It trains reconstructed values with binary cross-entropy on terminal outcomes, then uses them in PPO. For Qwen3-8B-Base, it reaches 45.9% in-domain mean accuracy versus PPO’s 37.5%, and 69.7% versus 67.6% out-of-domain; results cover tested verifiable tasks and models up to 9B.

hot.title: Construction of Simple Quadrangulations of the Sphere at Skeletal Joints
hot.summary: The authors construct joint quadrilateral layouts on a sphere by searching over candidate dual graphs and branch-direction assignments together, rejecting crossing arcs and incompatible cyclic orders. This avoids building the layout one branch at a time. For one six-direction example, their layout is crossing-free and convex, unlike two incremental methods; tests across sampled inputs show convexity is not universal.

hot.title: Read the Room Before Your Model Generates
hot.summary: Scenario-Actor selects a prompt-level sampling temperature from an inferred communicative scenario rather than using one global setting. It embeds prompt hidden states, then geometrically combines temperatures associated with five axes across nine scenario labels. Against nearest-centroid lookup, it improves AlpacaEval LC-WR from 27.10% to 30.03%. On task-only GSM8K prompts, accuracy is 65.28%, below greedy decoding and fixed T=0.5.

hot.title: PixelMoE: Scaling Pixel-Space Diffusion with LLM-Style Mixture-of-Experts
hot.summary: PixelMoE generates class-conditional ImageNet-1K images in pixel space, using token-selected experts and a two-stage resolution schedule. In a 100-epoch comparison, its large model reaches FID 1.78 with 632M active parameters, versus the dense baseline’s FID 2.95 with 622M active parameters. At 256×256, PixelMoE reports FID 1.47. These results support the approach only in this benchmark and setup.

hot.title: ForceWAM: Decoupling Future and Response Learning from Demo and Play Data for Contact-Rich Manipulation
hot.summary: ForceWAM predicts future wrist-camera images and force/torque trajectories for a task, while learning action responses from successful demonstrations and exploratory play. It updates actions using measured wrench feedback between slower future updates. In force-regulated sliding, it achieves 85% success, versus 40% with task-only training and 20% for the strongest external baselines. Rates span 85% to 95% across four tested conditions.

hot.title: Thinker-WM: A Unified World Model with Shared Multimodal Representations for Embodied Intelligence
hot.summary: Thinker-WM jointly models RGB video, metric depth, and executable robot actions in a shared dynamics transformer, with separate encoders and decoders. Depth interaction becomes bidirectional after pretraining. EWMBench Overall is 4.66, versus 4.60 for Qwen-RobotWorld. On RoboTwin turn_switch simulation, bidirectional RGB-depth interaction yields 75.0% success versus 60.0% for RGB-only. Real-robot closed-loop effectiveness remains unestablished.

hot.title: Cowork-Gym: Synthesizing Interactive Work Environments at Scale
hot.summary: Cowork-Gym generates environments for agents working with people through shared files and tools. It builds tasks, workspaces, user policies, and hybrid checks, then runs and revises environments; simulated users respond to progress and can change inputs. Qwen models improve in most comparisons; Ours-27B scores 0.8400 on PawBench under OpenClaw, but WildClawBench is a weakness and the pool is not representative.

hot.title: RoboSimStudio: An Interactive Toolkit for Rapid Real2Sim of Robot Manipulation Tasks
hot.summary: RoboSimStudio supports editable simulations of real tasks. People or coding agents adjust physics, run tasks, and use simulator-state feedback to revise models and behavior. In a sponge-wiping pilot, an agent verified a simulation in 56 minutes. GaP improved simulated wiped area from 0% to 100% over 14 iterations; its policy completed the task on a real robot, with agreement assessed qualitatively.

hot.title: Mixture of GFlowNets
hot.summary: MoGX trains generative flow networks (GFlowNets)—samplers that produce candidates in proportion to reward—to specialize across a reward landscape. A shared classifier shapes each sampler’s target, while trajectory exchange routes samples to components. In genomic ideotype design, MoGX found 39% of 1,024 optima at K=64, versus 31% for independent agents and 20% for data-parallel training; this measures simulated coverage, not crop yield.

hot.title: AReaL-RSI: Adaptive Scaling and Coordination of Recursive Self-Improvement
hot.summary: AReaL-RSI coordinates persistent AI research campaigns by assigning specialized researcher roles, routing evidence with its conditions and uncertainty, and reviewing campaigns to revise procedures for later teams. In KernelBench, sharing plus roles produced the lowest latency in all seven successful comparable task–backbone pairs, beating independent four-agent exploration by 1.9–27.5%. This tested-parallelism result does not establish matched-compute efficiency or cross-campaign gains.

hot.title: EvoSpatial: Experience-Driven Skill and Tool Evolution for Spatial Reasoning Agents
hot.summary: EvoSpatial stores reusable spatial procedures as skills linked to callable tools, preserving when steps apply and what evidence to check. It uses online evolution to revise this library from execution records and local checks, without benchmark labels. With Gemma4-31B, it averages 63.9% across 20 benchmarks, versus SpatialClaw's 59.9%; on BLINK, it scores 74.8%, below the no-tool baseline's 75.7%.

likes.title: RoboJEPA: Scaling Robotic Latent World Models
likes.summary: RoboJEPA predicts future visual features under robot actions and uses imagined outcomes to plan toward a goal image. Its predictor scales from 22 million to 8 billion parameters while keeping the V-JEPA 2.1 encoder fixed. A second-order compute law extrapolates held-out prediction error better than a standard power law, but does not establish a universal link to robot success.

likes.title: Long-WAM: Scaling the Context of World-Action Models
likes.summary: Long-WAM trains a robot controller to predict future video from visual history, then uses those predictions to generate actions. On RoboCasa GR-1, robot-domain autoregressive initialization raises success from 66.3% with 2.4 seconds of history to 78.7% with 19.2 seconds, while bidirectional initialization stays near 62%. This simulated comparison supports, but does not prove, the explanation that autoregressive pretraining helps use history.

likes.title: MiMo-V2.6: Scaling Reinforcement Learning Towards Self-Improvement
likes.summary: The authors train coding agents with groupwise grading, comparing attempts at the same task to add quality signals to binary test rewards. Online Groupwise Advantage Redistribution shifts positive credit toward higher-quality passing patches. MiMo-V2.6-Pro’s reported average pass-rate score across three sampled attempts rises from 58.4 to 72.6 on DeepSWE v1.1, but this mixed-task run does not isolate grading or compute effects.

likes.title: Embodied Turing Machines: Stateful Code for Robot Recursive Self-Improvement
likes.summary: COAP represents scene state in code and uses a fixed task program to choose actions, check outcomes, and update its records. At test time, it uses camera images and robot measurements without a model service. On RoboDojo, it reaches 70.24% overall success, versus 31.38% for PhysicalRSI. Results are from simulation and depend on state measurement and code robustness.

likes.title: Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervision
likes.summary: MASS improves open-ended research agents by having model copies coordinate through task-specific workflows, then fine-tuning their shared model on selected orchestrator and subagent trajectories. After two cycles, it achieves 1.2–1.6 times the base model’s score per output token on four research benchmarks. This does not extend to coding benchmarks, where the reported ratios are 0.96 and 0.94.

likes.title: Video Prediction Policy 2: Predict Better, Act Better
likes.summary: VPP2 develops a robot-control system that first predicts complete, instruction-grounded manipulation events, then trains an action model to use those predicted futures. It fine-tunes and distills a video model for fast prediction before learning action chunks. On real-world ALOHA trials, it averages 58.5% success across 10 categories, but ALOHA was represented in training; benchmark results also involve task-specific post-training.

likes.title: A Balanced Data Diet: Addressing the Exploration Bottleneck in Mega-Scale RL for Robot Control
likes.summary: Success Guided Sampling (SGS) allocates training episodes across a fixed set of task configurations according to recent success rates, emphasizing situations with intermediate success while retaining nonzero sampling probability for all configurations. In settings, it improves results: Anymal-D locomotion reaches 73% success at 1 million environments, versus 54% with PLR. Hardware nut-and-bolt transfer succeeds in 18 of 48 trials.

likes.title: Next-Concept Modeling: Fast, Parallel Coarse-to-Fine Text Generation
likes.summary: NCM generates text by encoding it into hierarchical discrete representations and predicting them coarse to fine, with codes at each level generated in parallel. It reports LM1B generative perplexity of 93.05 at 12 function evaluations, compared with DUO’s 97.30 at 128, alongside similar measured diversity and a reported 21× wall-clock speedup. These results are benchmark-specific, and larger-scale behavior remains open.

likes.title: LeWAM: End-to-End World and Action Modeling with JEPAs
likes.summary: LeWAM jointly learns how actions change a scene and which actions are plausible, then uses proposed actions to plan manipulation. Its model predicts latent states and action distributions, refining candidate sequences against a goal. Across ten simulated tasks, it averages 93.5% success versus 50.9% for LeWM with CEM. These results concern task-specific goal reaching from offline data, not broad transfer.

likes.title: Can Jev be Your Q or Policy in Reinforcement Learning?
likes.summary: The paper tests frozen Jev as guidance within reinforcement-learning training: as an action reference, exploration judge, and replay rater. Across nine MiniGrid tasks and three Atari games, learners sometimes outperform direct Jev control. Results depend on task and supplied information; in FourRooms, direct Jev succeeds in 96% of episodes with engineered navigation features, versus 40% without them.

likes.title: RSIGym: A Flexible Environment for Recursive Self-Improvement
likes.summary: RSIGym provides reusable services for training, inference, rollouts, evaluation, and sandbox computation, while permissions let agents change data, training settings, harnesses, or combinations. In one budgeted run, six agents improved 29 of 30 settings across five benchmarks. Opus 5 achieved an RSI-Index of 0.4809 and raised SWE-bench Verified from 17.67% to 50.33%. The results do not establish progress across later cycles.

likes.title: AgentGarten: Code Worlds for Evolving Agents
likes.summary: Interactive virtual worlds allow agents to learn through exploration and interaction. What agents can learn is bounded by the environments they practice in, which must be faithful, with consistent state, rules, and dynamics, and realistic, with observations that follow the real-world visual distributions. Achieving both across diverse worlds remains a bottleneck. We introduce AgentGarten, a framew

likes.title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
likes.summary: RSI-Anything uses predicted outcomes to select actions for testing, then pairs predictions with observed results to guide policy updates and conditional world-model adaptation. With the coder fixed on CodeContests, hidden-test all-pass success rose from 26.3% with a static verifier to 29.2% with fixed-model selection and 31.2% with adaptation, at similar online test usage. This does not establish sustained joint improvement.

likes.title: SuperNav: An Agentic Navigation System for Any Task in Any Scene
likes.summary: SuperNav uses a pretrained multimodal large language model (MLLM) to navigate environments across single-object, ordered multi-object, and demand-driven tasks. A harness provides tools, reusable Skills, task state, and context management; the model selects destinations while an executor handles motion. On 150 Habitat-GS single-object tasks, its Geo-based Executor achieves 78.00% success versus UniNaVid's 34.00%, supporting the complete system only in tested settings.

likes.title: Prior or Feedback? What an LLM Uses When Adapting Neural Operators
likes.summary: The authors test LLM tuning of a Fourier neural operator (FNO) using hosted DeepSeek-V4 Pro over 20 trials. It achieves lower held-out test nRMSE in all 36 runs against random search and 35 of 36 against TPE. Its first proposal beats 91.7% of random configurations; replay shows choices respond to score assignments, but not that feedback improves test performance.

likes.title: EmbodiedRSI: Active Continual Robot Learning Through Hypothesis-Guided Co-Evolution
likes.summary: EmbodiedRSI adapts a robot harness around a frozen vision-language-action model by maintaining competing code and skill hypotheses, selecting simulator experiments for expected information gain relative to cost, and retaining useful evidence. On RoboCasa365’s Composite-Unseen suite, it reports 71.3% success, versus 40.1% for Harness VLA. This supports harness-level adaptation on tested tasks, not model learning or universal gains.

likes.title: TokenRouter: Efficient Serving System for Token-Level LLM Routing
likes.summary: TokenRouter serves inference with per-token routing between language models, using asynchronous subservers and delayed batch admission. Developers define routing and state handoffs; each model server buffers arrivals and uses a throughput model to select a threshold. On R2R’s AIME setup at concurrency 4, it reports 244.56 generated tokens/s versus 89.62 for official R2R, a serving-efficiency result under routing assumptions.

likes.title: BrickBench: Evaluating Agentic Brick Design
likes.summary: BrickBench evaluates whether coding agents can turn written prompts into LEGO assemblies that meet construction checks and depict the requested scene. In BrickAgent, agents select parts, place them through compatible connectors, render builds, and revise them using validation feedback. GPT-6 Astra scores 1.00 on overall validity and 0.954 on VQA, but stability is simulated and does not establish real-world strength.

likes.title: SGF+: Decoupling Gradient Flows for Autoregressive Video Generation
likes.summary: SGF+ separates the context writer and denoiser with distinct parameters while retaining differentiable key-value states and the shared future-generation objective. It addresses conflicting role updates measured in SGF, where mean gradient angles were 104.2° in Attention and 106.3° in feed-forward networks. At 240 seconds, it scores 98.21 versus SGF’s 97.72 for subject consistency; reported 24-hour generations are qualitative examples.

likes.title: ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State
likes.summary: ReplaySSM reduces recurrent-state writes during state-space model decoding by keeping a checkpoint and buffering recent inputs, then periodically folding them into the checkpoint. It also supports pointer-based speculative rollback and separate low- and high-precision checkpoints. At batch size 256, whole-model decode latency improved 1.20–1.47× across four hybrid models; gains depend on setup and batch size, and checkpoint reads remain.
